# Effectiveness of the Adjuvanted Recombinant Zoster Vaccine in Adults ≥50 Years in the United States _Open Access_
## Abstract
Background
Recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) was approved for adults aged ≥50 years in the United States to prevent herpes zoster (HZ) and postherpetic neuralgia (PHN). This study evaluated real-world vaccine effectiveness (VE) of RZV in adults aged ≥50 years.
Methods
Among N = 102 766 (median age 68 years) who received 2 RZV doses (4 weeks–6 months apart), 48 028 (46.7%) had previously received zoster vaccine live; aVE was 73.9% (95% CI: 71.8%–75.8%) for HZ and 83.7% (95% CI: 75.1%–89.3%) for PHN. VE against HZ was comparable across individuals with concomitant vaccinations and different comorbidities.

...

Conclusions
Two doses of RZV were effective in preventing HZ and PHN in adults aged ≥50 years, with durable protection. These findings underscore the importance of adhering to the recommended vaccination schedule.

...

Although pre-licensure randomized trials showed high RZV efficacy  [9 , 10 ], further effectiveness studies are needed  [11–13 ]. The reported 2-dose RZV effectiveness against HZ ranged between 70.1% (68.6%–71.5%) and 74% (73%–76%) in ≥65-year-olds and between 76% (75%–78%) and 85.5% (83.5%–87.3%) in ≥50-year-olds  [14–17 ].

...

The overall adjusted 2-dose RZV effectiveness in this study was 73.9% (71.8%–75.8%) over 4 years of follow-up (mean 2.5 years), whereas the previously reported values in adults aged ≥50 years were 83.5% (74.9%–89.2%) (median 2.0 years of follow-up)  [15 ], 85.5% (83.5%–87.3%) (median 7.0 months of follow-up)  [16 ], and 76% (75%–78%) (mean 3.2 years of follow-up in unvaccinated and 1.4 years in 2-dose vaccinated individuals)  [17 ].

results.title: Efficacy and safety of the recombinant zoster vaccine: A systematic review and meta-analysis - ScienceDirect
excerpts:
# Efficacy and safety of the recombinant zoster vaccine: A systematic review and meta-analysis
## Abstract
Twenty three publications reporting on 14 studies were selected, including 2 pivotal RCTs in older immunocompetent adults (ZOE-50 and ZOE-70), 4 RCTs on immunocompromised patients (haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), haematological malignancies, solid tumour, and renal transplantation), and 8 observational studies.
Vaccine efficacy of RZV against herpes zoster (HZ) and postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) was very high in immunocompetent older adults (respectively 94% and 91.2% in adults ≥50 years and 91.3% and 88.8% in adults ≥70 years). However, the number needed to vaccinate (NNV) was relatively high (between 32 and 36 for HZ and between 261 and 335 for PHN).

The pooled vaccine effectiveness of recombinant zoster vaccine against herpes zoster for immunocompromised people was 64·3% (95% CI 61·4–67·0).

# Review
## 3. Results
For the immunocompetent subgroup, seven cohort studies were included in the meta-analysis. Five studies enrolled adults aged 50 years or older; of the remaining two, one included participants aged 40 years or older, and one was restricted to adults aged 65 years or older. The pooled vaccine effectiveness of the recombinant zoster vaccine against herpes zoster was 80·0% (95% CI 74·1–84·5; Fig. 3 ).
In adults aged 50–59 years, three studies were included in the meta-analysis, and the pooled effectiveness of recombinant zoster vaccine against herpes zoster was 72·6% (95% CI 54·8–83·3). Four cohort studies provided estimates for adults aged 60–69 years and 70–79 years; the pooled effectiveness was 76·4% (95% CI 61·8–85·4) and 78·5% (95% CI 66·9–86·0), respectively.

## DISCUSSION
The RZV was approved for adults aged 50 and over following the results of the ZOE-50 study. In this trial, RZV had an overall efficacy between 96.6% and 97.9% among all age groups 50 and above  [17 ]. In a follow-up study in individuals aged 70 and above (ZOE-70), RZV efficacy was 89.8%  [27 ].

# Zoster Recombinant Vaccine: Efficacy, Safety, and Duration
The recombinant zoster vaccine, sold under the brand name Shingrix, is a two-dose vaccine designed to prevent shingles (herpes zoster) and its complications in adults aged 50 and older.

...

## Efficacy in Clinical Trials
The vaccine’s headline numbers come from two large phase 3 trials known as ZOE-50 and ZOE-70, which together enrolled tens of thousands of adults. In ZOE-50, which included adults aged 50 and older, overall vaccine efficacy against shingles was about 97%, with efficacy between roughly 97% and 98% across all age groups studied. ² PubMed.
[Efficacy of an adjuvanted herpes zoster subunit vaccine in older adults](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25916341/) Combined data from both trials confirmed that protection exceeded 90% in every age group from 50 upward, including people in their seventies and eighties. ³ Clinical Infectious Diseases.

...

## How Long Protection Lasts
The final analysis of that follow-up study extended the picture even further. In adults who were at least 50 when first vaccinated, efficacy was about 80% during the extended follow-up period. Protection against the most feared complication, postherpetic neuralgia (persistent nerve pain after shingles), was about 88%.
